hints: A stretch that wraps around the end is the whole ring minus a stretch in the middle that you leave out. Which middle stretch would you want to leave out?
Run Kadane twice: once for the best normal stretch, once for the smallest (most negative) stretch. The best wrapping stretch is total − minStretch.

1. Compute total, the max-sum stretch maxS and the min-sum stretch minS in one pass.
  2. If maxS < 0, every number is negative: return maxS.
  3. Otherwise return max(maxS, total - minS).

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every start and every length up to n, walking around the ring.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Kadane for max and min at the same time; the answer is the better of a normal stretch and total minus the worst middle stretch.

explain: For [6,-4,-8,3,5]: total = 2, the best normal stretch is 8 ([3,5]) and the worst stretch is −12 ([-4,-8]). Wrapping gives 2 − (−12) = 14, i.e. [3,5,6] around the end. When all values are negative, total − minS would mean choosing an empty stretch (0), which is not allowed, so we return maxS instead, e.g. −2 for [-2,-5].
recognize: Max subarray sum on a circular array → max(Kadane max, total − Kadane min).
